elements.element: The liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Sections 9.1 and 9.2 impose substantively parallel caps on IBM and Customer.

elements.element: The cap uses the greater of a fixed-dollar amount and a fee-based amount.
elements.evidence: Each cap is the greater of $100,000 or the applicable twelve-month charges.

elements.element: The fixed-dollar limb of the cap is USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The fixed-dollar limb is only $100,000.

elements.element: The fee-based limb includes fees paid or payable.
elements.evidence: The clause includes only charges paid by Customer, not charges payable.

elements.element: The fee-based limb is measured over the 12 months preceding the claim.
elements.evidence: The clause measures the period before accrual of the first claim related to the Services, rather than before each relevant claim.

elements.element: Indirect damages are mutually excluded.
elements.evidence: The clause states that neither party will be liable to the other for indirect damages.

elements.element: Consequential damages are mutually excluded.
elements.evidence: The clause states that neither party will be liable to the other for consequential damages, including lost profits or savings.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is mutually carved out from the cap on an uncapped basis.
elements.evidence: The added sentence provides that the limitations in Sections 9.1 and 9.2 do not apply to a party's breach of its confidentiality obligations.

elements.element: Breach of data protection obligations is mutually carved out from the cap on an uncapped basis.
elements.evidence: No carve-out addresses data protection obligations.

elements.element: Breach of security obligations is mutually carved out from the cap on an uncapped basis.
elements.evidence: No carve-out addresses security obligations.

elements.element: Indemnification obligations are mutually carved out from the cap on an uncapped basis.
elements.evidence: For each party, indemnification payments are listed separately from the capped category of 'other actual direct damages,' with no monetary ceiling stated for indemnification.

elements.element: Gross negligence is mutually carved out from the cap on an uncapped basis.
elements.evidence: The added sentence provides that the limitations do not apply to a party's gross negligence.

elements.element: Wilful misconduct is mutually carved out from the cap on an uncapped basis.
elements.evidence: The added sentence provides that the limitations do not apply to a party's willful misconduct.

elements.element: Fraud is mutually carved out from the cap on an uncapped basis.
elements.evidence: There is no fraud carve-out; the broad cap language instead applies regardless of the basis of the claim and expressly includes misrepresentation.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is mutually carved out from the cap on an uncapped basis.
elements.evidence: No operative language carves out direct infringement of the other party's intellectual property.

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations are not treated as damages for purposes of the liability cap.
elements.evidence: The payment proviso says Section 10 does not apply to Customer's failure to pay, but it does not state or clearly establish that payment obligations are outside the caps in Sections 9.1 and 9.2 or are not damages for cap purposes.

elements.element: The liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Sections 9.1 and 9.2 impose substantively parallel caps on IBM and Customer.

elements.element: The cap amount is 12 months' fees.
elements.evidence: The operative amount is the greater of $100,000 or twelve months' charges paid, so it is not a cap equal solely to twelve months' fees.

elements.element: Indemnification obligations are mutually carved out from the cap.
elements.evidence: Each party's indemnification payments are listed separately from the capped category of 'other actual direct damages' and have no stated monetary ceiling.

elements.evidence: The added sentence makes the limitations in Sections 9.1 and 9.2 inapplicable to a party's breach of its confidentiality obligations.

result.reason: The redline adds the required mutual confidentiality, gross-negligence, and willful-misconduct carve-outs, and indemnification is structurally outside the capped category. However, neither level is complete: the operative cap remains the greater of $100,000 and twelve months' paid charges, rather than the preferred $1,000,000 formula or the fallback cap of twelve months' fees. The preferred data-protection, security, fraud, IP-infringement, and payment-treatment requirements are also absent. The redline additionally inserts language completing a separate third-party-claims exclusion and relocates a confidentiality fragment, so it changes more than necessary and affects an unrelated liability allocation. Drafting quality is reduced by unresolved fragments, numbering inconsistencies, and ambiguity about the scope of the payment proviso.
